title: Scaling LLM Training Using RDMA over Converged Ethernet
problem: InfiniBand traditional for HPC but expensive; RoCE offers cost-effective alternative but scaling performance unclear
motivation: Large-scale LLM training demands high-bandwidth networking; commodity Ethernet + RDMA provides cost savings
method: The researchers tested whether RoCE (RDMA over Converged Ethernet—a technique for efficiently moving data using regular network cables) could match the performance of the more expensive InfiniBand networking standard when training large language models at scale. They systematically benchmarked different training configurations: splitting the workload across multiple computers (data sharding), representing numbers with fewer bits (quantization), recalculating values instead of storing them (recomputation), and adjusting how many examples are processed together (batch sizing). By measuring how well these approaches worked on both RoCE and InfiniBand, they identified the settings where RoCE achieves similar scaling efficiency.
key_novelty: RoCE (RDMA over Converged Ethernet, a cheaper networking approach using regular cables) achieves near-linear scaling—where speed improves proportionally as you add more computers—matching the performance of InfiniBand when properly configured.
contributions: Benchmarks RoCE scaling for LLM training
Provides guidance on data sharding strategies
